papers.title: QLCoder: A Query Synthesizer For Static Analysis of Security Vulnerabilities

task.summary: CodeQL query synthesis from CVE metadata

method.summary: CVE-grounded retrieval, AST guidance, CodeQL LSP tools, and iterative execution feedback

evidence.result: Correct-query rate 53.4% versus 10% for Claude Code-only; F1 0.70 versus 0.048 for IRIS and 0.073 for CodeQL suites.
evidence.source_location: Official abstract, main evaluation, and artifact paper environment
evidence.caveats: Security-query synthesis is narrower than general software engineering.

papers.title: RPG: A Repository Planning Graph for Unified and Scalable Codebase Generation

method.summary: Persistent graph over features, functions, files, interfaces, and data flow with graph-guided generation and validation

evidence.result: ZeroRepo coverage 81.5% versus Claude Code 54.2% and Codex 28.4%; pass rate 69.7% versus Claude Code 33.9%.
evidence.caveats: ZeroRepo uses o3-mini while the Claude Code baseline uses Claude 4 Sonnet, so model and harness effects are mixed.

papers.title: Comparing AI Agents to Cybersecurity Professionals in Real-World Penetration Testing

task.summary: Long-horizon penetration testing in a live enterprise network

method.summary: Supervisor with dynamic expert agents, recursive task decomposition, parallel exploration, context management, triage, and reporting

evidence.result: ARTEMIS found 9 valid vulnerabilities with an 82% valid-submission rate, ranked second overall, and outperformed 9 of 10 human participants.
evidence.caveats: Runtime limits, model combinations, safety refusals, and product policies differ across systems.

papers.title: MLZero: A Multi-Agent System for End-to-end Machine Learning Automation

task.benchmark: MLE-Bench Lite and Multimodal AutoML Agent Benchmark

method.summary: Hierarchical agents with multimodal perception, semantic and episodic memory, and a planning-coding-evaluation loop

evidence.result: MLZero led MLE-Bench Lite with six gold medals and achieved 0.92 success on its multimodal benchmark; one appendix setting reports 6.5% errors versus 26.9% for Codex CLI.
evidence.source_location: Abstract, main benchmark results, and appendix error analysis
evidence.caveats: Results concern machine-learning automation and should not be generalized to all software-engineering tasks.

papers.title: FormAct: Agentic Source Editing for Rich-Format Document Generation

method.summary: HTML source editor, template retrieval, rendered-page review agent, iterative refinement, and edit-triggered context compression

evidence.result: Render correctness 4.81 versus 4.39 for multi-pass Codex; human rank-1 rate 0.760 versus 0.140.
evidence.source_location: Main comparison table and review-refinement ablation
evidence.caveats: Codex has slightly higher content alignment, and the task is document formatting rather than source-code repair.

papers.title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses

method.summary: Closed-loop harness evolution using component, trajectory, and decision observability with evidence-backed edits and rollback

evidence.result: Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 improves from 69.7 to 77.0, above a human-designed Codex-CLI harness at 71.9; transfer uses 12% fewer tokens on SWE-bench Verified.
evidence.source_location: Abstract and Terminal-Bench 2 transfer and ablation results
evidence.caveats: Preprint; model, harness, and evaluation-budget effects require careful separation.

papers.title: WebDesignIter: Co-Evolving Design Knowledge for Repository-Level Front-End Code Generation

method.summary: Persistent architecture and design knowledge graph, design-informed planning, targeted patches, and sandbox repair

evidence.result: Average Pass@2 improves by 9.55 percentage points over existing baselines; removing design knowledge reduces Pass@1 by 11.4 points.
evidence.source_location: Abstract, main Web-Bench comparison, and design-knowledge ablation
evidence.caveats: Front-end-specific benchmark and preprint status.

papers.title: Prefactory: Automated Discovery and Application of Library-Adoption Refactorings

task.summary: Discovery and application of library-adoption refactorings

method.summary: LLM-synthesized lexical and structural search heuristics, deterministic candidate ranking, targeted refactoring, and differential tests

evidence.result: File-level detection 75 versus Codex 35; function-level detection 56 versus 32; 40 of 56 candidates yield test-validated refactorings.
evidence.source_location: Abstract and PrefactoryBench detection and validation results
evidence.caveats: The strongest comparison concerns candidate detection, not universal end-to-end task success.

papers.title: RustPrint: Documentation-Guided Agentic Codebase Migration from C to Rust

task.summary: Whole-codebase migration from C to Rust
task.benchmark: Eight real C repositories from 11K to 84K lines of code

method.summary: Architecture documentation blueprint, module and data-flow planning, compile feedback, documentation mismatch repair, and source-test translation

evidence.result: In the reported Kimi-K2-Instruct setting, feature preservation is 93.26% versus 52.52% for agentic Claude Code; cross-evaluation test pass is 95.17% versus 79.85%.
evidence.source_location: Abstract and feature-preservation and cross-evaluation results
evidence.caveats: The comparison mixes model and scaffold choices and is specific to C-to-Rust migration.

papers.title: RepoOMP: Repository-Aware Hotspot OpenMP Parallelization via Dependency-Aware Context Reduction

method.summary: Multi-granularity dependency graph, rule-or-LLM hotspot routing, reduced transformation context, and compile/workload/speedup validation

evidence.result: Across nine detailed kernels, speedup improves 18% to 28% and token cost falls 47% to 68% relative to unstructured Claude Code.
evidence.caveats: Domain-specific high-performance-computing task and preprint status.

papers.title: Unlocking Model Potentials Through Adaptive Multi-Agent Scaffolding for Efficient Issue Resolution

method.summary: Event-based agent communication, issue-quality routing, parallel patching and validation, and exploratory fallback

evidence.result: SWE-bench Verified improves 3.6 to 8.4 percentage points and SWE-bench Pro 6.3 to 18.5 points; average cost is $1.18 lower than multi-agent Claude Code.
evidence.source_location: Abstract and SWE-bench Verified and Pro comparisons
evidence.caveats: Exact model parity varies by reported configuration; preprint.

papers.title: When Parallelism Pays Off: Cohesion-Aware Task Partitioning for Multi-Agent Coding

method.summary: Static dependency graph partitioning, structural hub isolation, community detection, and dependency-aware scheduling

evidence.result: Pass rate improves 14.0%, wall-clock speedup reaches 2.10x, and API cost falls 35% relative to Claude Code Agent Teams and simpler schedules.
evidence.source_location: Abstract and DevEval and CodeProjectEval comparisons
evidence.caveats: Small 28-task evaluation and preprint status.

papers.title: On the Impact of AGENTS.md Files on the Efficiency of AI Coding Agents

task.summary: Real pull-request tasks with and without repository instructions

method.summary: Persistent repository-level build, test, style, and directory guidance in AGENTS.md

evidence.result: Median runtime falls 28.64% and output tokens fall 16.58% with comparable completion behavior.
evidence.caveats: Workshop study and configuration intervention rather than a standalone agent.

papers.title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents

method.summary: GRPO-trained 14B retrieval agent that issues multi-turn parallel grep, glob, and read operations for a frozen downstream coding agent

evidence.result: Resolve rate 27.0% versus 25.8% without retrieval; resolved tasks use 15% fewer rounds and 19% fewer tokens.
evidence.caveats: The clean numeric comparison is against a frozen no-retrieval downstream agent, not necessarily the released Claude Code CLI.

papers.title: SCATE: Learning to Supervise Coding Agents for Cost-Effective Test Generation

method.summary: Contextual-bandit supervisor that selects testing actions from current coverage and testability state

evidence.result: Line coverage improves 32.3% and branch coverage 30.9% over agent-only Gemini CLI; adaptation is also evaluated with Claude Code.
evidence.caveats: The abstract does not provide an equally complete numeric head-to-head against Claude Code.

papers.title: Terminal-Bench 2.0: Advancing Agentic Terminal Intelligence through Better Evaluation and Verification

method.summary: Evaluation-only benchmark with stronger task verification and a neutral terminal scaffold

evidence.result: GPT-5.2 with Codex CLI scores 62.9; Claude Opus 4.5 scores 57.8 with Terminus 2 and 52.1 with Claude Code.
evidence.source_location: Main agent and model results table
evidence.caveats: Benchmark result; differences can reflect both model and harness, and no new method is proposed to beat the products.

papers.title: BountyBench: Dollar Impact of AI Agent Attackers and Defenders on Real-World Cybersecurity Systems

method.summary: Evaluation-only benchmark of offensive and defensive cybersecurity agents

evidence.result: Codex o3-high detects 12.5% and patches 90%; Claude Code patches 87.5% and exploits 57.5% in the reported settings.
evidence.source_location: Official abstract and agent task-results tables
evidence.caveats: Benchmark-only evidence across different tasks and model configurations.

papers.title: Engineering Pitfalls in AI Coding Tools: An Empirical Study of Bugs in Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI

task.summary: Empirical analysis of product bug reports

method.summary: Evaluation-only manual taxonomy of functionality, integration, invocation, and command-execution failures

evidence.result: More than 67% of studied bugs concern functionality; API, integration, and configuration account for 36.9% of root causes.
evidence.source_location: Abstract and root-cause, symptom, and workflow-stage findings
evidence.caveats: Failure-taxonomy study; it does not propose an agent that outperforms the products.

papers.title: Interactive Code Generation via Test-Driven User-Intent Formalization

method.summary: Generate tests to formalize user intent, collect lightweight feedback, and rank or prune candidate programs

evidence.result: With one to five simulated user queries, Codex pass@1 gains 22.49 to 37.71 points on MBPP and 24.79 to 53.98 points on HumanEval.
evidence.caveats: This is the historical OpenAI Codex model, not the modern Codex CLI product.

papers.title: Towards Iterative End-to-End Software Development: A Feature-Driven Multi-Agent Framework

task.benchmark: APPDev, 15 Android applications with 8 to 26 functional requirements

method.summary: Feature-driven multi-agent development with a dependency DAG, layered business/design/code context, iterative implementation, and build repair

evidence.result: With Claude 4 Sonnet, EvoDev reaches 100% build success and 3.57 function completeness versus 73.3% and 2.27 for Claude Code, a 57.3% relative completeness gain.
evidence.caveats: APPDev contains 15 Android apps and uses manual quality scoring; EvoDev takes about twice Claude Code's wall-clock time in the Claude 4 Sonnet comparison.

papers.title: Red-Teaming Coding Agents from a Tool-Invocation Perspective: An Empirical Security Assessment

task.summary: Prompt exfiltration and tool-invocation hijacking in production coding agents
task.benchmark: Six real-world coding agents and 25 agent-model configurations

method.summary: Tool-call schema pressure for prompt leakage followed by a two-channel injection through tool descriptions and returns

evidence.result: ToolLeak obtains the best pseudo-recall on 18 of 25 real agent-model pairs; the follow-on attack hijacks all six studied agents, including a Claude Code RCE case study.
evidence.source_location: ISSTA 2026 official abstract; Tables 3 to 5 and Sections 6 to 7
evidence.caveats: Claude Code is an attack target rather than a baseline to beat; results depend on product and backend versions that may change quickly.

papers.title: To Run or Not to Run: Analyzing the Cost-Effectiveness of Code Execution in LLM-Based Program Repair

task.summary: Repository-level program repair with and without local code execution
task.benchmark: 200 SWE-bench Lite and Verified instances; 3,000 controlled runs

method.summary: Paired five-arm execution-policy ablation spanning prohibited, quota-limited, budget-guided, and unrestricted execution

evidence.result: Disabling execution changes resolve rate by only 1 to 3 points for Claude Code and Codex in the main cells, while saving 56 to 62% of tokens and 48 to 54% of wall-clock time for Claude Code.
evidence.source_location: ISSTA 2026 paper, Tables 2 to 4 and Sections 4.2 to 4.3
evidence.caveats: The prompt-level prohibition was not perfectly obeyed by Claude Code, though the paper separately measures and hard-checks unintended execution.

papers.title: Mining Tactics for Automated Theorem Proving

task.summary: Automated theorem proving in Rocq projects
task.benchmark: 6,199 theorems across CompCert, Coq-Art, Ext-Lib, and VFA

method.summary: LLM-mined reusable symbolic tactics, validity and generalization checks, and integration into CoqHammer

evidence.result: Mined tactics let CoqHammer prove 23.87% more theorems; integrating the improved prover with Claude Code increases the overall number proved by 9.90%.
evidence.caveats: The public conference record does not report the Claude Code version, backbone model, absolute theorem counts for the product ablation, or budget parity.

papers.title: AgentRadio: Passive Awareness for Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Collaboration

method.summary: Four Claude Code agents coordinated through asynchronous threads, messages, passive mention watching, and a five-phase negotiation protocol

evidence.result: AgentRadio reaches 62.1% task accuracy versus 32.3% for single-agent Claude Code; a near-cost six-run baseline reaches 37.9%, and single-agent Opus 4.8 reaches 57.2%.
evidence.caveats: The four-agent method costs about six times a single Opus 4.6 run, although the paper includes a near-cost resampling baseline.

papers.title: Do Context Files Help Coding Agents? A Two-Agent Ablation Study on Real Repositories

task.summary: Repository repair under different persistent-context strategies
task.benchmark: 17 real tasks from three Python repositories; 288 evaluated runs

method.summary: Within-task comparison of no context, always-on AGENTS.md, and selectively retrieved repository wiki context with gold tests and equivalence testing

evidence.result: Claude Code pass rates are 53.3%, 55.6%, and 55.6%; Codex rates are 58.8%, 56.9%, and 52.9%, with no detectable strategy effect and bounded null effects of 10 to 15 points.
evidence.caveats: Only three Python repositories are studied; Claude and Codex receive injected context through different channels, and two selective-context corpora are larger than AGENTS.md.

papers.title: Guardrails Beat Guidance: A Large-Scale Study of Rules, Skills, and Persistent Configuration for Coding Agents

task.summary: Repository repair under persistent rule-file configurations
task.benchmark: SWE-bench Verified; more than 5,000 Claude Code runs

method.summary: Paired rule-file experiments over source, count, polarity, type, and composition, backed by a corpus of 25,532 rules

evidence.result: Random and expert-curated rule files both reach 63.8% pass rate versus 50.0% with no rules; only negative constraints are individually beneficial in the reported ablation.
evidence.caveats: Results are limited to Claude Code with Opus 4.6 on a discriminative Python subset; several headline pairwise differences do not reach conventional significance.

papers.title: LCM: Lossless Context Management

method.summary: Lossless message storage, hierarchical summary DAGs, deterministic recursive compression, and engine-managed parallel map operators

evidence.result: Volt averages 74.8 versus 70.3 for Claude Code and wins at every tested context length from 32K to 1M tokens, with gaps up to 12.6 points.
evidence.caveats: OOLONG may be contaminated in Opus 4.6, and the paper does not provide a matched end-to-end cost comparison for LCM's auxiliary calls.

papers.title: Context-Augmented Code Generation: How Product Context Improves AI Coding Agent Decision Compliance by 49%

task.benchmark: DCBench, eight tasks with 41 weighted decision points and 48 runs

method.summary: Retrieval over recorded product decisions, personas, customer signals, and competitive context during specification and implementation

evidence.result: Decision compliance rises from 19/41 (46%) for Claude Code to 39/41 (95%) with Brief; cost per merge-ready task falls 68% despite 28% higher total spend.
evidence.caveats: The augmented arm adds Opus planning, a longer timeout, generated specifications, tests, and retrieval, so the 49-point gain is not attributable to product context alone.

papers.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?

products.model: Claude Opus 5 and DeepSeek V4 variants
GPT-5.6, GLM 5.2, Nex N2, and Qwen 3.5 variants

method.summary: Three-paradigm benchmark with private tests, a scientific failure taxonomy, and paired ablations of explicit scientific guidance

evidence.result: The best configuration, Claude Code with Opus 5 at max effort, reaches 47.90% Pass@1; no evaluated agent crosses 50%, and scientific guidance helps some models but hurts others.
evidence.caveats: Results span different models, harnesses, and reasoning settings; the paper is a benchmark and failure analysis, not a method that beats the products.

papers.title: SWE-Bench Mobile: Can Large Language Model Agents Develop Industry-Level Mobile Applications?

task.summary: Industry-scale iOS feature development from PRDs and Figma designs
task.benchmark: 50 tasks over a 500,000-line Swift and Objective-C production codebase

method.summary: Multimodal mobile benchmark with private tests, cross-agent model controls, cost analysis, prompt ablations, and error taxonomy

evidence.result: Across 22 configurations, the best task success is 12%; the same Opus 4.5 model varies by up to 6x across agents, and a defensive-programming prompt raises Claude Code test pass from 19.3% to 26.7%.
evidence.caveats: The public artifact URL reported in the PDF was unavailable during review; product results vary across models and include MCP-assisted visual access.

papers.title: SEC-bench Pro: Can Language Models Solve Long-Horizon Software Security Tasks?

task.summary: Long-horizon proof-of-concept synthesis for disclosed vulnerabilities
task.benchmark: 344 validated V8, SpiderMonkey, and Linux kernel vulnerabilities

method.summary: Self-evolving reconstruction pipeline, three-image execution oracle, and LLM judge for vulnerability-specific PoC attribution

evidence.result: Codex with GPT-5.5 solves 58% of all instances; Claude Code with Opus 4.6 times out often but solves most completed attempts, while GLM-5 solves 13 of 344.
evidence.caveats: The configurations use different models and completion behavior; this is comparative capability measurement rather than a proposed system beating a product baseline.

papers.title: Harnessing Code Agents for Automatic Software Verification

task.summary: Fully automatic proof construction for verified software
task.benchmark: 4,257 Iris lemmas, 217 Rust-library lemmas, 318 reglang theorems, and 72 Lean-port lemmas

method.summary: A reusable harness that lets the code agent choose whole-proof strategy while prover kernels enforce soundness, completeness, retries, and termination

evidence.result: Aria proves all 4,257 targeted Iris lemmas, all 217 Rust-library lemmas, all 318 reglang theorems, and 72 not-yet-ported Lean lemmas; prior reglang provers manage about one in eight.
evidence.source_location: Abstract, Tables 1 and 3 to 4, and Sections 4 to 6
evidence.caveats: Claude Code is the host harness, not a separately measured baseline; comparisons to prior provers mix models, systems, and compute budgets.
